title: Left inverses of a matrix up to a scalar and its maximal minors
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n\ge m\ge0$ integers, $A$ an $n\times m$ matrix with entries in $R$ [def-weil-matrix], and $J\subseteq R$ the ideal generated by the $m\times m$ minors of $A$, i.e. by the determinants $\det(A_I)$, $I\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$, $|I|=m$, where $A_I$ is the $m\times m$ submatrix [def-weil-submatrix] formed by the rows of $A$ with indices in $I$ (for $m=0$, $J=R$, the empty minor being $1$). (1) For every $f\in J$ there is an $m\times n$ matrix $B$ over $R$ with $BA=f\cdot1_{m\times m}$. (2) If $f\in R$ and $B$ is an $m\times n$ matrix over $R$ with $BA=f\cdot1_{m\times m}$, then $f^m\in J$; explicitly $f^m=\sum_{|I|=m}b_I\det(A_I)$ with $b_I$ the determinant of the $m\times m$ matrix formed by the columns of $B$ with indices in $I$ (Cauchy–Binet).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07DQ (lemma-matrix-left-inverse, line 2668) and its proof (adjugates of the A_I for (1); the Cauchy-Binet formula, item-cauchy-binet, for (2)); used for Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07ET (lemma-parse-equation-strictly-standard-one)

proof.text: For each size-m subset I, put e_I = orderEmbOfFin(I) and let E_I be the identity matrix on Fin n restricted to rows e_I. Mathlib Matrix.one_submatrix_mul gives E_I A = A_I [def-weil-matrix, def-weil-submatrix]. This construction also makes sense when m = 0.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07DQ (lemma-matrix-left-inverse, line 2668)

proof.text: For each generator det(A_I), the matrix adj(A_I) E_I has product with A equal to det(A_I) times the identity, by associativity, step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-adjugate-identity]. Apply Submodule.span_induction to membership in J. The property of having a scalar left inverse is closed under zero (choose the zero matrix), addition (add the two witness matrices) and scalar multiplication (scale the witness matrix). Matrix.add_mul, Matrix.smul_mul, add_smul and smul_smul verify these closure steps. Thus every f in J has the required scalar left inverse. This is the ideal-combination argument of Stacks 07DQ expressed by induction rather than by choosing coefficients; no data is chosen from an unproved existence theorem.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07DQ (lemma-matrix-left-inverse, line 2668)

proof.text: (Part (2): the determinant of $f\cdot1$.) Let $B$ be $m\times n$ with $BA=f\cdot1_{m\times m}$. Then $\det(BA)=\det(f\cdot1_{m\times m})=f^m$: in the Leibniz expansion $\det(f\cdot1)=\sum_{\sigma\in S_m}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{k}(f\delta_{\sigma(k),k})$ only $\sigma=\mathrm{id}$ gives a nonzero term, namely $f^m$ (for $m=0$ both sides are $1$).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07DQ (lemma-matrix-left-inverse, line 2668)

proof.text: (Part (2): Cauchy–Binet.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cauchy-binet] to the $m\times n$ matrix $B$ and the $n\times m$ matrix $A$: $\det(BA)=\sum_{|I|=m}\det(B^{I})\det(A_I)$, where $B^{I}$ is the $m\times m$ matrix formed by the columns of $B$ with indices in $I$ and $A_I$, the matrix formed by the rows of $A$ with indices in $I$, is the one of the statement. With step 3 and $b_I:=\det(B^{I})$ this gives $f^m=\sum_{|I|=m}b_I\det(A_I)$, an $R$-linear combination of the generators of $J$, so $f^m\in J$. (The hypothesis $n\ge m$ is not used in (2); if $n<m$ the sum is empty and $f^m=0\in J$.)

lean.statement: theorem scalar_left_inverse_maximal_minors {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (n m : ℕ) (_hmn : m ≤ n) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin m) R) : let J : Ideal R := Ideal.span (Set.range (fun I : {I : Finset (Fin n) // I.card = m} ↦ (A.submatrix (I.val.orderEmbOfFin I.property) id).det)) (∀ f : R, f ∈ J → ∃ B : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) R, B * A = f • 1) ∧ (∀ (f : R) (B : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) R), B * A = f • 1 → f ^ m ∈ J ∧ f ^ m = ∑ I : {I : Finset (Fin n) // I.card = m}, (B.submatrix id (I.val.orderEmbOfFin I.property)).det * (A.submatrix (I.val.orderEmbOfFin I.property) id).det)

reviewed_lean.note: CommRing R (zero ring ok), n m : ℕ with m ≤ n, A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin m) R; J = Ideal.span of det (A.submatrix orderEmbOfFin id) over card-m subsets (m=0: span{1}=⊤); (1) f ∈ J → ∃ B, B * A = f • 1; (2) B * A = f • 1 → f^m ∈ J ∧ Cauchy–Binet sum with B column minors, same indexing as landed Matrix.cauchy_binet; no hollow hyps, one universe, no private copies, not in Mathlib
